subject: Save data from the first and last day

messages.subject: Save data from the first and last day
parts:
Hi all, 

I am a beginner in GGIR and am currently processing accelerometer data collected by the Axivity wrist band and am having a problem with the analysis and would like to get your answer.

In the data analysis length I have set a minimum wear of 16 hours as a criterion, but I also want to keep the data from the first and last day of data collection, although they do not meet the 16 hour criterion. Following the instructions in the manual, I have modified excludefirstlast for part 2 and minimum_MM_length.part5 for part 5, but the problem has not yet been solved, so I hope I can get your reply and help, thanks!

Here’ the code:

###

Library (GGIR)

g.shell.GGIR(#-------------------------------

             # General parameters

             #-------------------------------

             mode= c(1,2,3,4,5),

             datadir= "D:/gg/",

             outputdir= "E:/817/",

             f0 = 1,

             f1 = 1,

             overwrite = FALSE,

             do.imp=TRUE,

             idloc=1,

             print.filename=FALSE,

             storefolderstructure = FALSE,

             #-------------------------------

             # Part 1 parameters:

             #-------------------------------

             windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),

             do.cal=TRUE,

             do.enmo = TRUE,

             do.anglez=TRUE,

             chunksize=1,

             printsummary=TRUE,

             #-------------------------------

             # Part 2 parameters:

             #-------------------------------

             strategy = 1,

             ndayswindow= 7,

             hrs.del.start = 0,

             hrs.del.end = 0,

             maxdur = 7,

             includedaycrit = 16,

             L5M5window = c(0,24),

             M5L5res = 10,

             winhr = c(5,10),

             qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),

             qwindow=c(0,24),

             ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),

             mvpathreshold =c(100),

             #-------------------------------

             # Part 3 parameters:

             #-------------------------------

             timethreshold= c(5,10),

             anglethreshold=5,

             ignorenonwear = TRUE,

             #-------------------------------

             # Part 4 parameters:

             #-------------------------------

             excludefirstlast = FALSE,

             includenightcrit = 16,

             def.noc.sleep = 1,

             outliers.only = FALSE,

             criterror = 4,

             relyonsleeplog = FALSE,

             sleeplogidnum = FALSE,

             colid=1,

             coln1=2,

             do.visual = TRUE,

             #-------------------------------

             # Part 5 parameters:

             #-------------------------------

             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses

             threshold.lig = c(45),

             threshold.mod = c(100),

             threshold.vig = c(430),

             excludefirstlast = FALSE,

             boutcriter = 0.8,

             boutcriter.in = 0.9,

             boutcriter.lig = 0.8,

             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,

             boutdur.in = c(10,20,30),

             boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10),

             boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),

             timewindow = c("WW","MM"),

             minimun_MM_length.part5 = 10,

             includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3,

             #-----------------------------------

             # Report generation

             #-------------------------------

             do.report=c(2,4,5))

## End(Not run)

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Save data from the first and last day
parts:
Hi Zhang,

If the first or last day does not have at least 23 hours of data in the MM window analysis, it will be excluded. This is intentional. Motivation: including incomplete days will distort the time-use variable average across days.

Imagine calculating time spent in inactivity (sedentary behaviour if you like) for a person who consistently does it  for 14 hours per day each day of the year. For the first and last recording day you may miss half of the day, by which you would only capture 7 of those 14 hours. If you include those incomplete days the final average across all the days you would get ((7 x 2) + (14 x 5)) / 7 = 12 hours, which is not correct because the true behaviour of the person is 14 hours per day.

This is why time-use analysis should always rely on complete days with a low amount of non-wear or have a clever way of imputing the missing hours using imputed behavioural patterns. GGIR currently does not have that, and I am not sure it even exists yet. If this would be added, we could be more flexible with the inclusion of days.

Another solution is to collect more recording days.

For waking-up to waking-up (WW) window analyses in part 5, the first or last day may additionally be excluded because no reliable estimate can be made of waking-up time to define the edge of those days.

Best,

Vincent
